 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 27012020 at about 5.15 p.m., the Petitioner was travelling as a passenger in an Auto bearing No.KA545195 near Doddabala Hippermara Nagamangala to Bindiganavele road, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District and the driver of the said Auto was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner.
At that time, Auto bearing Regn.No.KA06C3164 driven by its driver came from opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Petitioner's auto and caused the accident.
Due to the said accident, the Petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Government Hospital, Bindiganavele for first aid treatment and thereafter he was shifted to AIMS Hospital, B.G.Nagar,
wherein, he took treatment as an inpatient.

He has spent more than Rs.1,00,000/
towards medical treatment, conveyance and nourishments.
Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as an agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

The Respondent No.1 and 2 are the RC owners of the Auto bearing No.KA06C 3164 and KA545195 respectively and the Respondent No.3 is the insurer of the Auto and all the Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.

sentences.text: In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 remained absent.
Hence he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 and 3 appeared before the court through their counsels and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement, the Respondent No.2 has denied age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending auto bearing No.KA545195.
Further he has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the said accident and the expenses for the treatment of the Petitioner.
Further he contended that he is not the necessary party as the charge sheet has not filed against his vehicle.
The I.O. has filed charge sheet against the Auto bearing No.KA06C3164.
Hence, he is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, among these and other grounds, the Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the Petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.3, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving by the driver of auto bearing No.KA545195.
Further it denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.

Further it has contended that the accident has occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Auto bearing Reg. No.KA06C3164 and charge sheet was filed against the Auto bearing Reg. No. KA06C3164.
Hence it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, among these and other grounds, Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
4. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.

2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?
3. What Order or Award ?
5. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked 11 documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.11.
He also examined one witness as P.W.2 and got marked 2 documents as per Ex.P12 to P.15 and closed his side evidence.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked 10 documents as per Ex.R.1 to 10.
Respondent No.3 got examined its Administrative Officer as RW.2 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.11 and R.12 and closed its side evidence.

6. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondents and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available Ramesh.K.N vs Sathisha on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185934549/
3 on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :
 REASONS 7. Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Motor Vehicle accident that occurred on 27012020 at about 5.15 p.m. due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the auto bearing Regn.No.KA06C3164 and Auto bearing Reg. No.KA 545195.
8.

On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 and 3 have denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Auto bearing No.KA545195.
9.
In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined a witness as P.W.2 and got marked 15 documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex
P.W.1 has re iterated the Petition averments in his chief affidavit.
Ex.P1 to Ex.P8
are the True copies of FIR with Complaint, Spot Panchanama, Seizer Panchanama, IMV Report, Wound certificate, Notice u/s 133 of MV Act, Statement of witnesses and Charge sheet.
Ex.P.9 is the Discharge summary, Ex.P.10 is the Aadhar card and Ex.P.11 is the Medical bills.

10. Upon going through Ex.P.1 FIR with Complaint, it shows that on the complaint lodged before Bindiganavile Police Station, the PSI of the concerned Police Station has registered the case against the driver of the Auto bearing Reg.No.KA06C 3164 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279,
337 of IPC.
Ex.P2 is the Spot Panchanama and Ex.P.3 is the Seizure Panchanama which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P.4 is the IMV report which shows that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of both the vehicles involved.
Ex.P5 is the Wound Certificate of the Petitioner which shows that the Petitioner had sustained tenderness and deformity in the Right thigh and abrasion in the Right knee joint 1 x 1cm.
Ex.P.6 is the Notice under Section 133 of MV Act.
Ex.P.7 is the Statement of witnesses.

Ex.P8 is the Certified copy of the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the PSI of Bindiganavile Police Station has submitted Charge sheet against the driver of the offending Auto bearing Reg. No.KA06C3164 for the offences punishable under Sec.279,337, 338 of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act.

11. Upon going through the Chargesheet i.e., Ex.P8 Column No.17 reads as under:

Further, P.W.1 examined Dr.B.G.Sagar as P.W.2 and he also reiterated about the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a RTA.
PW.1 is subjected for crossexamination by the Learned Counsel for Respondent No.2 and 3.

In the cross examination PW.1 admitted that complaint was lodged against the driver of the Auto bearing Reg. No.KA06C3164 and charge sheet was also filed against the driver of the Auto bearing No.KA06C3164.

Further Ex.p.8 i.e., charge sheet clearly shows that after thorough investigation, I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the Auto bearing Reg. No.KA 06C3164.
13.

Further, Respondent No.2 being the owner of Auto bearing No.KA545195 got examined himself as RW.2 and got marked Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.10 i.e., Certified copies of Complaint, FIR, IMV Report, Plea of the accused in CC No.398/2020, Order Sheet in CC No.398/2020, Notarized Copy of DL of Hemaraju B., Notarized Copy of RC of vehicle bearing No.KA549195, Certificate of Fitness,
Original Insurance Policy and Attested Copy of Extract of DL of P.Hema Raju.
Ex.R.4 and Ex.R.5 i.e., Plea and Order sheet in C.C.No.398/2020 shows that the driver of Auto bearing No.KA06C 3164 by name Venkatesh had pleaded guilty and paid fine.
Further Ex.R.8 and Ex.R.9 are FC and Policy which also shows that it was valid at the time of accident.
14. Respondent No.3 examined its witness by name Himendra as RW.3 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.R.11 and Ex.R12.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and the deposition and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the accident is caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Auto bearing Reg.No.KA06C 3164.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the 'Affirmative'.
15.
Issue No. 2

: As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the offending Auto bearing Reg. No.KA06C3164 by its driver, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
16. In the Petition, the Petitioner has shown his age as 35 years.
He has produced Aadhar Card at Ex.P.10 to prove his age.
As per the Adhaar card i.e. Ex.P.10, the date of birth of the Petitioner is shown as 12.06.1985.
The accident taken place on 27.01.2020.

Hence, the age of the Petitioner, as on the date of accident was 35 years and the same is to be taken for consideration.
Ramesh.

K.N vs Sathisha on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185934549/
5 17.
Further, the petitioner has averred that he was working as agriculturist and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
In this regard, he has not produced any document to show that he was earning Rs.20,000/ p.m.

Therefore, in the absence of any income proof, this Tribunal is of the opinion that, since the accident has been occurred in the year 2020, the notional income to be assessed as per the guidelines of the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority i.e. 14,500/ p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
19.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P5 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Tenderness and deformity in the right thigh.
2. Abrasion in the right knee joint 1 x 1 cms.
Xray of right thigh with knee joint reveals fracture of distal third of the right femur.
Further, the Doctor has opined that injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES :
20. Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs. 30,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
21.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted as an inpatient from 27.01.2020 to 24.02.2020 at Adichunchanagiri Hospital.
Further, P.W.2 Dr.B.G.Sagar has also reiterated the same in his evidence.

22. Upon going through Ex.P.9 i.e., the Discharge summary which shows that the Petitioner was admitted as an inpatient from 27.01.2020 to 24.02.2020 at Adichunchanagiri Hospital i.e., totally for 29 days.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as inpatient is 29 days.
23. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as three months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.43,500/ under this head (@ Rs.14,500/ per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S Ramesh.K.N vs Sathisha on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185934549/
6
CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :

24. Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.9,000/ (@ Rs.100/ per day) towards attendants charges, Rs.9,000/
towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.9,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.

In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 27,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
25. The Petitioner has deposed that he spent more than Rs.1,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 30 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.11.
I have gone through the medical bills and the same are acceptable of Rs.31,093.50/.
Hence, by rounding off the same, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.31,100/as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :
26. The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he has suffered permanent disablement and cannot work as earlier.
Even in his evidence, P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
27. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr. B.G.Sagar as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked Inpatient records, Permanent disability certificate, Outpatient records and CT Scan films at Ex.P.12 to P.15.
He assessed the disability of the Petitioner to the extent of 40.89%.
28. PW.2 has admitted in his cross examination that the fractures are united.
He has also admitted that as per the Wound Certificate only tenderness and abrasions are appear.

29. Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on record and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 10% would be just and proper.
30. As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 16.

With multiplier of 16, income of Rs.14,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 10%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,74,000/ (Rs.14,500/ x 12 =1,74,000/, Rs.1,74,000/x 16 x 10/100 =2,78,400/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs. 2,78,400/ under this head.

Ramesh.K.N vs Sathisha on 21 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185934549/
7

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
31.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 30,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 30,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 27,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 31,100/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 43,500/ laid up period 6. Loss of Future income Rs. 2,78,400/ Total Rs. 4,40,600/ Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.4,40,000/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

32. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA 06C3164.
Further the charge sheet at Ex.P.8 shows that the alleged offending vehicle does not had insurance policy at the time of the accident.
Therefore the Respondent No.1 being the owner of the offending Auto bearing Reg. No. KA06C3164 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

Further Respondent No.2 being the RC owner of the Auto bearing Reg. No. KA06C3164 and Respondent No.3 being the insurer of the offending Auto bearing Reg. No. KA 06C3164 are not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
33. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner against the Respondent No.1 U/Sec. 166 of M.V. Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioner of M.V. Act is hereby dismissed.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation as stated supra to the Petitioner.

The Petitioner is entitled for  Compensation of Rs.4,40,000/ along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation as stated supra to the Petitioner.
Ramesh

8
The Respondent No.1 being the RC owner of the offending vehicle, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

After being deposit of the Award amount and interest by the Respondent No.1, 75% of the award amount is ordered to be paid to the Petitioner by way of E payment and after proper identification and the remaining 25% of the award amount shall be kept in Fixed deposit in his name in any Nationalized or Scheduled Bank for a period of 3 years of his choice.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs. 1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
